# 05-final-validation: Validate the upgraded solution

Run restore and a full solution build for `simulator.sln`, then inspect the resulting project graph and runtime outputs for missing references, resource regressions, native asset problems, package conflicts, and residual binding redirect configuration. Because test coverage was skipped, document that no generated behavioral baseline was run and capture any remaining manual verification recommendations.

**Done when**: The complete solution restores and builds without errors, all 9 projects target the intended .NET 8 framework variant, no incompatible package or legacy binding redirect remains, and residual risks or deferred recommendations are documented.

## Research Findings

- Scope is `simulator.sln`, which contains exactly 9 projects. The evaluated dependency graph is: `Commons` -> `SimulatorUI`, `ModuleAPI`; `ModuleAPI` -> `DNP3PluginAPI`, `DefaultOutstationPlugin`, `RelayOutstationPlugin`, `DNP3Module`, and `Simulator`; `DNP3PluginAPI` -> `DefaultOutstationPlugin`, `RelayOutstationPlugin`, `DNP3Module`; `DNP3Commons` -> `DefaultOutstationPlugin`, `RelayOutstationPlugin`, `DNP3Module`; `DefaultOutstationPlugin` and `RelayOutstationPlugin` -> their respective shared APIs; `DNP3Module` -> all DNP3/plugin dependencies; `Simulator` -> `Commons`, `DNP3Module`, `ModuleAPI`, and `SimulatorUI`.
- Current solution TFMs are `Commons=net8.0`; `ModuleAPI`, `DNP3PluginAPI`, `DNP3Commons`, `DefaultOutstationPlugin`, `RelayOutstationPlugin`, `DNP3Module`, `SimulatorUI`, and `Simulator=net8.0-windows`. All are single-targeted; no solution project retains `TargetFrameworks` multi-targeting.
- In-solution package declarations use `opendnp3 3.1.2`; `DNP3Module` additionally uses `System.IO.Ports 8.0.0`, and `SimulatorUI` uses `System.Resources.Extensions 8.0.0`. A legacy, unreferenced duplicate `simulator/DNP3/DNP3Commons/DNP3Commons — kopia.csproj` plus `packages.config` still references `opendnp3 2.2.0-M1` and `net45`/`v6.0.8`; it is outside `simulator.sln` and will be reported, not changed here.
- No `bindingRedirect`, `assemblyBinding`, `oldVersion`, or `dependentAssembly` entries were found in active project configuration. `Simulator/App.config` and `SimulatorUI/App.config` retain legacy `<supportedRuntime ... sku=\".NETFramework,Version=v4.5\"/>` metadata and require manual runtime review/removal if generated outputs still copy it.
- Runtime/resource audit found 38 `.resx` files with embedded binary/System.Drawing resources. Native `opendnp3` assets exist under `packages/opendnp3.3.1.2/runtime/x64` and `runtime/x86`; active projects specify `PlatformTarget=x64`. Runtime verification must confirm the x64 adapter/interface DLLs are copied or discoverable beside the executable.
- Planned checks: explicit `dotnet restore simulator.sln`, full `dotnet build simulator.sln` with captured error/warning counts, evaluated TFM/project graph inspection, assets/package conflict review, binding redirect search, resource/native asset verification, and output assembly existence checks. Test baseline is intentionally skipped because `scenario-instructions.md` selects `Test Coverage: Skip`.

## Decomposition Verdict

This is atomic final validation: it audits one solution after all migration tasks and does not modify independent projects, package APIs, or source paths. Evaluated `execution.md`, `breakdown-hints/common.md`, and `breakdown-hints/framework-migration.md`; multi-project dependency-ordering, package-replacement, stub-resolution, System.Web, and Windows API isolation decomposition triggers do not apply to this read/restore/build audit. Required building-projects, managing-target-frameworks, modifying-project-properties, and WinForms build guidance were also loaded.
